title: Feed a pencil into a moving sharpener while turning its crank
instruction: Sharpen one end of the yellow pencil. Gradually feed it into the front opening while turning the rear crank clockwise until it has a complete point. Withdraw the pencil, place it across both rests, let go, and move both hands clear.
context: Manual pencil sharpening is recognizable household and classroom tool use. The physical coordination is simultaneous axial feeding of a loose workpiece and continuous rotation of a free-spinning crank knob by the other hand. A guided moving fixture provides a repeatable disturbance. Empty crank rotation earns no credit.
setup: Use the calibrated bimanual YAM station, with world X forward, Y left, Z up in metres; tabletop Z=0.7475 and arm bases at (0,+/-0.305,0.750). All initial body rotations are identity. Eight objects: (1) A 5.0 kg ballasted guided stage has body origin (0.245,-0.040,0.7625). Its base is 0.180 x 0.140 x 0.030 m; its support post is 0.025 x 0.050 x 0.055 m, offset (0,0,+0.0425) m. A world Y guide permits +/-0.020 m travel. The commanded Y is -0.040+0.005*sin(2*pi*t/8) m. (2) A 0.500 kg blue rigid sharpener housing, 0.060 x 0.070 x 0.070 m, is fixed to the stage at (0.245,-0.040,0.8675). Four rectangular bars form a genuine 0.009 x 0.009 m square through-aperture along X. The front face is X=0.215 m. (3) A 0.080 kg red crank carrier rotates freely about X at (0.285,-0.040,0.8675); it consists of an X-axis hub of radius 0.008 m and length 0.018 m, an 0.008 x 0.012 x 0.043 m arm offset Z=-0.0175 m, and an X-axis 0.003 m radius, 0.040 m long spindle offset (+0.020,0,-0.035) m. Passive angular damping is 0.006 N m s/degree free and 0.026 N m s/degree while cutting, capped at 0.08 N m. (4) An 0.008 kg black free-spinning X-axis knob, radius 0.008 m and length 0.030 m, starts at (0.331,-0.040,0.8325), attached to the crank with a passive revolute joint; its damping is 0.00573 N m s/rad capped at 0.005 N m. Crank radius is 0.035 m. (5) The 0.005 kg grey cutter-face surrogate, 0.003 x 0.008 x 0.008 m, starts at (0.232,-0.040,0.8675). It is on a passive X slider relative to the housing, travel 0 to 0.024 m, spring 780 N/m, damping 3 N s/m, force cap 8 N, initial spring rest at zero. The effective cutter face retreats by the actual material cut depth, up to 18 mm. (6) A blunt yellow round wooden pencil, radius 0.0035 m, length 0.140 m and mass 0.006 kg, lies along X at (0.120,0.100,0.7810). (7-8) Two fixed grey 0.016 x 0.040 x 0.030 m rests are centred at (0.055,0.100,0.7625) and (0.160,0.100,0.7625). Generated geometry dimensions, joint anchors and fixture CAD are in assets/geometry.json and assets/fixture.scad. Start both grippers open in READY, seed 0, zero object jitter and motion phase zero.
scoring: 0.25 at a taper of at least 6 mm; 0.50 at 12 mm; 0.75 at an intact 18 mm taper with exposed graphite; 1.00 when that pencil also rests across both supports, released, with both hands over 100 mm clear for 1 s. The simulation can cut up to 2.4 mm per net clockwise turn and only while the aligned pencil physically compresses the current cutter spring 1.4–5.0 mm. Cut depth cannot exceed current measured axial insertion past first contact minus the minimum compression. Empty cranking and fixed-depth turning cannot reach any positive tier from reset. Each end has its own cut depth. The exact return tolerances are in the protocol. A pencil more than 30 mm below the tabletop scores zero. For physical grading, confirm at least 6, 12 or 18 mm actual axial feed while turning in side video at the same taper tiers, using a witness band and ruler fixed to the housing. Measure the finished taper and graphite with a ruler or labelled close-up. No internal motion or force measurement is required to grade a real trial.
run_limit: 1,600 control steps (80 simulated seconds at 20 Hz)
reset_notes: Center the carriage, put the crank knob below its axis, and reset the cutter spring and both cut depths. Place a fresh blunt 140 mm pencil on the rests and start both arms ready with open grippers. For a physical trial, use an enclosed manual-feed sharpener, clear the shavings and calibrate the visible feed reference as described in the protocol.
fidelity: Native grasps, crank and spring contact require real axial feed as the effective cutter face retreats. The visible taper grows with measured insertion and loaded rotation. Spring and crank loads are nominal surrogates. The pencil retains its full-length collider; teeth, shavings and fracture are omitted. The demo commands robot joints with state feedback. Dream-1 uses standard observations.
scores: Dream-1 beta run: 0.00; scripted native-contact demo: 1.00
